cards.title: Future-First Thinking
cards.mirror: When clarity remains distant, could one modest step reveal useful information—or is more inquiry genuinely needed first?
cards.loop: Option: test one reversible step, then compare what became clearer with what remained uncertain.

cards.title: The Horizon Contract
cards.mirror: A direction may become actionable through commitment, while exploration can still reveal whether that direction deserves continued investment.
cards.loop: Option: make one time-limited commitment and observe whether it improves focus without closing useful discovery.

cards.title: The First Vector
cards.mirror: A first vector can turn an imagined future into something testable, though small movement does not guarantee a large shift.
cards.loop: Option: take the smallest meaningful step and record whether it changes information, access, or momentum.

cards.title: Future Noise
cards.mirror: When one concern repeats after facts are checked, notice whether it changes with timing, stakes, or available options.
cards.loop: Optionally, test one smaller, reversible version and record whether the same evidenced risk appears.

cards.title: The Pull
cards.mirror: A compelling future can feel gravitational, yet present desire must share the field with commitments, uncertainty, and limits.
cards.loop: Option: translate the pull into one chosen action, then check its fit with current responsibilities.

cards.title: Future Geometry
cards.mirror: The future’s sensed geometry may point toward values, constraints, habits, or relationships that deserve clearer names and practical tests.
cards.loop: Option: sketch the future shape, label its parts, and test one present-day implication.

cards.title: Future Friction
cards.mirror: Friction marks contact with a constraint; its source may be growth, poor fit, danger, or ordinary difficulty.
cards.loop: Option: reduce one friction point and observe whether the direction becomes safer, clearer, or less suitable.

cards.title: Future-Identity Lock
cards.mirror: A chosen future identity can steady decisions while remaining open to evidence, changing circumstances, and other legitimate roles.
cards.loop: Option: apply the chosen identity to one decision, then test whether it clarifies or distorts the choice.

cards.title: Future Compression
cards.mirror: A distant future may feel nearer when translated into present decisions, even while external timelines and dependencies remain unchanged.
cards.loop: Option: plan one week from the destination backward, then compare imagined compression with actual constraints.

cards.title: Future-Motion
cards.mirror: Momentum may feel future-driven while actually emerging through present choices, repeated habits, available support, and favorable conditions.
cards.loop: Option: repeat one small enabling action and observe which present factor actually sustains motion.

cards.title: Future Alignment
cards.mirror: Choosing a future identity may organize some present decisions without resolving every conflict, demand, or incompatible value.
cards.loop: Option: align one behavior with the chosen direction, then inspect what becomes clearer and what remains contested.

cards.title: Arrival
cards.mirror: An internal sense of arrival can change present posture without proving that external work, conditions, or consequences are complete.
cards.loop: Option: embody one quality of arrival briefly, then compare internal change with unchanged external requirements.

cards.title: First Resistance
cards.mirror: What becomes noticeable when the first step meets friction: hesitation, missing resources, unclear stakes, or a firm boundary?
cards.loop: Optionally test one smaller step, then compare whether friction softens, persists, or becomes more specific.

cards.title: Familiar Cage
cards.mirror: Familiarity can shelter, steady, or confine; its effect becomes visible in what it enables and repeatedly prevents.
cards.loop: Compare one familiar choice with a low-risk alternative, observing protection, cost, and available movement.

cards.title: Friction Map
cards.mirror: Recurring friction can form a map, but the pattern alone does not declare growth, danger, or direction.
cards.loop: Mark one repeated friction point, vary a condition, and observe whether strain, risk, or movement changes.

cards.title: Emotional Static
cards.mirror: When emotional intensity shifts across time or context, the static image invites comparison—not dismissal of a possible warning.
cards.loop: Optionally record the signal, pause, and compare it after one calmer interval.

cards.title: The Hidden Veto
cards.mirror: Repeated reversals, delays, or competing commitments can resemble a quiet veto without proving an unseen veto-maker.
cards.loop: Name two conflicting commitments, test one small choice, and observe which constraint actually appears.

cards.title: Instruction Layer
cards.mirror: Friction may contain usable information, though fatigue, fear, incompatible demands, barriers, and noise can look similar.
cards.loop: Adjust one plausible factor, then observe whether the resistance changes enough to clarify its source.

cards.title: Aligned Resistance
cards.mirror: A spike in resistance marks a moment for reassessment, not proof that alignment or breakthrough is near.
cards.loop: Pause one commitment level down and compare alignment, safety, capacity, timing, and consequences.

cards.title: Directional Fear
cards.mirror: Fear can highlight value, danger, uncertainty, conditioning, or overload; direction requires evidence beyond intensity alone.
cards.loop: Compare one feared option across value, concrete risk, reversibility, capacity, and available alternatives.

cards.title: Resistance Contract
cards.mirror: A recurring limit may resemble an old agreement when present choices repeatedly follow a once-useful rule.
cards.loop: Write one suspected rule, test a narrow exception, and compare consequences with the contract metaphor.

cards.title: Following the Edge
cards.mirror: Discomfort can mark learning, danger, depletion, coercion, or misalignment; the edge must be assessed before following.
cards.loop: Approach one low-risk edge briefly, with clear pause conditions, then compare capacity, consequence, and recovery.

cards.title: Resistance Compass
cards.mirror: Resistance may refine orientation when compared with values, evidence, constraints, safety, and consequences—not when followed alone.
cards.loop: Add one resistance signal to a five-input decision check, then test the smallest reversible direction.

cards.title: Instruction Accepted
cards.mirror: After an informed adjustment, friction may soften, persist, relocate, or reveal that no single instruction was present.
cards.loop: Try one evidence-based adjustment, then compare the resistance before, during, and after the change.

cards.title: Soft Drift
cards.mirror: Notice whether small, repeated departures from chosen direction are accumulating—or simply reflecting ordinary variation.
cards.loop: Optionally track one recurring choice for a week, then compare its direction and context.

cards.title: Micro-Abandonment
cards.mirror: Small departures from stated intentions may create disconnection, though changed priorities or constraints can look similar.
cards.loop: Optionally repair or renegotiate one small commitment, then observe whether consistency changes.

cards.title: Identity Vector
cards.mirror: Repeated choices can be read as a vector, while exploration may remain directionally useful rather than misaligned.
cards.loop: Name one provisional direction and test it against three upcoming choices.

cards.title: Leak
cards.mirror: The leak image may highlight neglected habits, boundaries, or environments that repeatedly interrupt a chosen direction.
cards.loop: Temporarily maintain one neglected point and observe whether recurring friction changes.

cards.title: Collapse Moment
cards.mirror: Some disruptions have recurring precursors, while others become legible only afterward or arrive without warning.
cards.loop: Choose one possible precursor and monitor it without assuming prevention is available.

cards.title: The Drift Signal
cards.mirror: Unease may accompany a loss of direction, but context must distinguish that signal from other sources.
cards.loop: Log one episode of unease, its context, and the decision it seems to concern.

cards.title: Identity Reclaim
cards.mirror: Reclaiming may mean renewing selected commitments, while changed commitments can also represent legitimate development.
cards.loop: Revisit one former commitment briefly and test whether it still provides orientation.

cards.title: Vector Collapse
cards.mirror: A missing future vector may contribute to stalled coordination, though resources, dependencies, or unclear information may matter more.
cards.loop: Set one provisional horizon and observe whether a stalled decision becomes easier to resolve.

cards.title: Identity Anchor
cards.mirror: Revisable commitments can anchor direction through routines, boundaries, or criteria without fixing one permanent future identity.
cards.loop: Try one anchor for a week, with a scheduled point for reconsideration.

cards.title: Identity Stabilization
cards.mirror: Stability may appear as continuity across changing conditions, while clarity can still refine what deserves continuity.
cards.loop: Hold one small practice steady while clarifying one uncertain decision.

cards.title: Identity Field
cards.mirror: The identity field can represent interacting environments, inputs, relationships, and norms that influence—but do not control—action.
cards.loop: Change one contextual input briefly, then compare the same task under both conditions.

cards.title: Identity Cohesion
cards.mirror: Cohesion may emerge when different aims coordinate without requiring every part to share one direction.
cards.loop: Map two competing aims and test one boundary that lets both remain visible.

cards.title: The Inner Deal
cards.mirror: A quiet bargain may be visible when action repeatedly depends on an unspoken condition.
cards.loop: Optionally name one condition and test a smaller version of the choice.

cards.title: Delay Negotiator
cards.mirror: “Later” can mark either useful timing or postponement without a clear decision point.
cards.loop: Try giving one delay a date, purpose, and decision criterion.

cards.title: Emotional Bargain
cards.mirror: Short-term calm may carry a cost when the same unspoken concern repeatedly returns.
cards.loop: In one low-stakes moment, test a measured statement of the concern.

cards.title: Split Council
cards.mirror: The council image may fit when stable priorities repeatedly pull the same choice in opposing directions.
cards.loop: Name two competing priorities and trial a choice that minimally serves both.

cards.title: Negotiated Identity
cards.mirror: Adaptation becomes worth examining when preferences and limits repeatedly disappear across roles, with recognizable costs afterward.
cards.loop: Test one low-stakes preference openly and observe both relational and practical effects.

cards.title: Terms & Conditions
cards.mirror: An implicit term may be present when the same “only if” pattern repeatedly stalls action.
cards.loop: Write one suspected if-then term, then test a limited exception.

cards.title: The Non-Negotiable
cards.mirror: A value, commitment, or current priority may need firmer terms—but each carries different costs.
cards.loop: Trial one scoped non-negotiable briefly, with an exception and review date.

cards.title: Emotional Gate
cards.mirror: The gate image may fit when a specific unresolved concern repeatedly accompanies stalled movement.
cards.loop: Pair one factual plan with one named concern and test a modest next step.

cards.title: Self-Against-Self
cards.mirror: Countervailing priorities may appear when building actions are repeatedly followed by reversals under similar conditions.
cards.loop: Track one build-and-reversal pair, then test a smaller step serving both priorities.

cards.title: Unified Terms
cards.mirror: Workable consent may matter when the same unresolved objection repeatedly reopens an otherwise settled plan.
cards.loop: Trial a minimum agreement while recording one dissent and scheduling its review.

cards.title: Aligned Negotiator
cards.mirror: Negotiation can serve a chosen commitment when exceptions and tradeoffs are tested against clear criteria.
cards.loop: Trial one future-facing boundary briefly, then review its benefits, costs, and exceptions.

cards.title: Internal Treaty
cards.mirror: A treaty can coordinate enduring differences without requiring every priority to move identically.
cards.loop: Draft a short, revisable treaty naming a shared aim, dissent, next step, and review.

cards.title: Sabotage Signature
cards.mirror: What repeating sequence appears before a chosen action gets delayed, reduced, or abandoned?
cards.loop: Optional: track one recurring sequence for a week without trying to fix it.

cards.title: The False Win
cards.mirror: Which satisfying wins also carry delayed costs for the direction that matters?
cards.loop: Optional: compare one immediate reward with its effects three days later.

cards.title: The Protector
cards.mirror: Could a recurring retreat be preserving something valuable, or simply reflecting present limits?
cards.loop: Optional: test one smaller step while preserving the suspected concern.

cards.title: Contract Anchor
cards.mirror: Does a repeated rule seem to anchor choices after its usefulness has faded?
cards.loop: Optional: name one suspected rule and suspend it for a low-stakes choice.

cards.title: Fear Clause
cards.mirror: What concern appears in the fine print when a planned step repeatedly narrows?
cards.loop: Optional: name one concern, then test a bounded version of the step.

cards.title: Countermove
cards.mirror: After visible progress, does a recurring countermove reduce, reverse, or complicate the next step?
cards.loop: Optional: watch the next milestone for one predefined countermove indicator.

cards.title: Contract Reveal
cards.mirror: When difficulty intensifies, what repeated rule or split becomes easier to observe?
cards.loop: Optional: pause during one pressure spike and record competing commitments without resolving them.

cards.title: Old Promises
cards.mirror: When recurring “shoulds” outpredict present incentives, might an old promise still be shaping the choice?
cards.loop: Optionally alternate two competing criteria across comparable low-stakes choices, then compare the outcomes.

cards.title: Loyal Sabotage
cards.mirror: When a familiar choice repeats, what observable duty might it preserve, and what would distinguish loyalty from familiarity, incentives, limited capacity, or uncertainty?
cards.loop: Optional: define one concrete duty, then compare matched, reversible forms with practical support held constant—one that visibly carries the duty forward and one that serves the immediate task without it.

cards.title: Contract Break
cards.mirror: What changes when an outdated agreement is replaced, and what patterns remain afterward?
cards.loop: Optional: revise one commitment and observe three related decisions before drawing conclusions.

cards.title: Aligned Loyalty
cards.mirror: Which loyalties reinforce chosen values, and which create observable conflict among commitments?
cards.loop: Optional: redirect one commitment toward a named value and review its actual effects.

cards.title: Sabotage Ends
cards.mirror: Does a chosen identity agreement add anything measurable beyond the same practical support used alone?
cards.loop: Optionally alternate practical support alone with the same support plus one explicit agreement.

cards.title: Time Gap
cards.mirror: Where does clear intention remain visible while action repeatedly begins later than expected?
cards.loop: Optionally test one low-risk step now against one deliberately scheduled step.

cards.title: Delay Window
cards.mirror: When a decision pauses, does the open window bring useful information or repeated drift?
cards.loop: Leave one pause open briefly, with a deadline and a question it must answer.

cards.title: Immediate Vector
cards.mirror: Which opportunities become clearer through a small trial, and which require verification before movement?
cards.loop: Test one promising direction with the smallest reversible action that can return useful evidence.

cards.title: Temporal Friction
cards.mirror: Does waiting make the task objectively harder, or does repeated anticipation make it feel heavier?
cards.loop: Compare one early micro-step with one intentional pause, then note what actually changes.

cards.title: Action Lapse
cards.mirror: An interrupted action can reveal a broken sequence without defining the person who began it.
cards.loop: Re-enter one paused sequence through a step small enough to stop or revise.

cards.title: Compression Line
cards.mirror: When does deliberation clarify a commitment, and when does it merely reopen a settled choice?
cards.loop: Give one recurring decision a criterion, a deadline, and one reversible committed step.

cards.title: Temporal Edge
cards.mirror: A temporal edge may appear when readiness increases, though uncertainty can still justify stepping back.
cards.loop: At one readiness threshold, test a reversible move or pause for one named uncertainty.

cards.title: Time Fold
cards.mirror: What present choice changes when an envisioned future is treated as a perspective, not a promise?
cards.loop: Borrow one criterion from an envisioned future and test it in a reversible present choice.

cards.title: Competing Timelines
cards.mirror: When two futures compete, which concrete priorities, costs, and commitments distinguish their paths?
cards.loop: Compare two paths using three criteria, then trial the more reversible option briefly.

cards.title: Accelerated Identity
cards.mirror: Speed may reinforce a chosen direction when the action is aligned, reversible, and responsive to feedback.
cards.loop: Accelerate one pre-checked action briefly, with a clear stop condition and feedback measure.

cards.title: Time Collapse
cards.mirror: A debate may close when its criteria are met, while new warning signals remain welcome.
cards.loop: Close one adequately considered choice until review, unless a named warning condition appears.

cards.title: Zero Distance
cards.mirror: How much of a distant future reflects present practice, and how much remains constrained by time and circumstance?
cards.loop: Practice one future-consistent behavior briefly, then compare aspiration with material conditions.

cards.title: First Fracture
cards.mirror: A first crack may mark change, or simply expose a temporary mismatch worth watching.
cards.loop: Optionally track one recurring crack for a week before assigning it a direction.

cards.title: Breakage Path
cards.mirror: A break can reveal pressure, but damage, chance, or external force may explain the same line.
cards.loop: Test one break as a clue, while keeping repair and disengagement equally available.

cards.title: Fracture Pulse
cards.mirror: Tension may carry useful information, though its apparent pulse can be brief, ambiguous, or unrelated to direction.
cards.loop: Briefly log three tension pulses, then compare what changed and what remained.

cards.title: Fracture Lens
cards.mirror: A fracture can act as a lens on demand, capacity, and fit without proving that something larger must emerge.
cards.loop: Temporarily reduce one demand and observe whether the fracture pattern changes.

cards.title: Breaking Point
cards.mirror: A breaking point may reveal limits or options, but it does not guarantee that breakthrough waits beyond it.
cards.loop: Try one brief pause at a limit and record what becomes observable.

cards.title: Fracture Map
cards.mirror: Break lines may form a partial map, especially when the same strain appears across time and contexts.
cards.loop: Trace three related breaks and check whether their apparent map survives comparison.

cards.title: Fracture Choice
cards.mirror: The next choice can shape a fracture’s course, alongside resources, timing, constraints, and other people’s actions.
cards.loop: Compare two reversible responses against present values, conditions, and likely costs.

cards.title: Fracture Stability
cards.mirror: Integration may support stability when repair restores function without concealing damage or transferring strain elsewhere.
cards.loop: Test one modest repair and monitor function, recurrence, and new strain.

cards.title: Threshold
cards.mirror: A threshold can invite movement or caution; repeated hesitation alone does not reveal which response fits.
cards.loop: Define one reversible crossing, then compare its information gain with its risk.

cards.title: Fracture Rhythm
cards.mirror: Some fractures recur with a rhythm, while others remain irregular events that resist a single sequence.
cards.loop: Time-stamp three breakpoints and compare their order, spacing, triggers, and recovery.

cards.title: Fracture Alignment
cards.mirror: A break may clarify a chosen direction, but relief or novelty can resemble alignment without confirming it.
cards.loop: Trial one value-linked step and watch whether contradictions lessen or multiply.

cards.title: Fracture Integration
cards.mirror: A fracture may reveal usable details, unresolved questions, or damage that offers little basis for rebuilding.
cards.loop: Sort one break into salvage, discard, and unknown; test only one salvageable element.

cards.title: Architect Awakening
cards.mirror: Where do recurring defaults leave room for deliberate design, and where do circumstances still set the frame?
cards.loop: Optionally redesign one recurring choice and observe whether agency increases without creating new friction.

cards.title: Structure Audit
cards.mirror: When effort repeatedly meets the same friction, which surrounding rule, cue, or constraint might be contributing?
cards.loop: Temporarily change one structural variable and compare the effort, errors, or delay that follows.

cards.title: Identity Blueprint
cards.mirror: Could a provisional blueprint clarify which roles, traits, directions, or boundaries deserve practical exploration?
cards.loop: Sketch one provisional identity feature, test it once, and revise it from the observed fit.

cards.title: Constraint Design
cards.mirror: Which revisable boundary might reduce conflicting choices, and which options remain necessary for learning or adaptation?
cards.loop: Try one removable constraint briefly, watching for reduced conflict, rigidity, or unintended cost.

cards.title: Architect Threshold
cards.mirror: A threshold may appear when a familiar response pauses long enough for one deliberate alternative to become visible.
cards.loop: Mark one recurring fork, try a different response once, and compare what changes afterward.

cards.title: Structural Identity
cards.mirror: Do calendar, environment, rhythms, and boundaries consistently support a stated direction, or require repeated renegotiation?
cards.loop: Adjust one supporting structure for a week and observe whether follow-through becomes steadier or merely different.

cards.title: System Author
cards.mirror: When a written goal repeatedly stalls at the same point, could a supporting system change the conditions?
cards.loop: Pair one goal with a tiny repeatable system, then compare starts, completions, and burden.

cards.title: Identity Geometry
cards.mirror: If commitments crowd or boundaries overlap, what does the geometry image reveal without treating discomfort as proof?
cards.loop: Sketch one crowded arrangement, move a boundary provisionally, and observe whether choices become clearer.

cards.title: Architect Conflict
cards.mirror: Across comparable choices, do familiar and emerging commitments preserve different benefits, or does context explain the alternation?
cards.loop: Try both options across several low-stakes choices; record immediate benefits, costs, and context.

cards.title: Structural Rewrite
cards.mirror: Which recurring arrangement sustains an old pattern, and how might a changed story interact with that structure?
cards.loop: Alter one arrangement while holding the stated story steady, then compare whether the pattern changes.

cards.title: Identity Architect
cards.mirror: Across recurring choices, does changing one cue alter later decisions, or do external conditions better explain the pattern?
cards.loop: Repeat one reversible cue change across several cycles and compare carryover with external conditions.

cards.title: Architect Seal
cards.mirror: Which commitments and supports currently work together well enough to mark a checkpoint without closing future revision?
cards.loop: Create a thirty-day provisional design, reviewing whether its supports remain coherent under changing conditions.

cards.title: Shadow Contract
cards.mirror: What unstated condition seems to precede the same choice, and could present constraints explain the pattern equally well?
cards.loop: Optionally name one possible term, then watch whether it predicts the next similar choice.

cards.title: Hidden Rule
cards.mirror: Does one recurring condition organize several choices, or do different situations appear to follow different rules?
cards.loop: Write one candidate rule and compare it with two recent examples.

cards.title: Shadow Loyalty
cards.mirror: Could a repeated choice be preserving loyalty, obligation, attachment, or continuity—and what other explanation fits?
cards.loop: Try one low-stakes variation and observe what the relationship actually requires.

cards.title: Unspoken Terms
cards.mirror: Which expectation seems active without being stated, and does naming it accurately describe what others actually do?
cards.loop: Draft one possible term privately, then compare it with the next interaction.

cards.title: Inherited Script
cards.mirror: Where does an old storyline appear in present choices, and where do current preferences or conditions explain more?
cards.loop: Try one alternate line in a reversible choice and compare the outcome.

cards.title: Shadow Obligation
cards.mirror: Which obligations are explicit, reciprocal, assumed, or imposed—and what evidence distinguishes them in practice?
cards.loop: Reclassify one nonurgent duty temporarily, then observe what consequences actually follow.

cards.title: Agreement Audit
cards.mirror: Could one recurring pattern be partly maintained by an agreement, while conditioning or constraint carries the rest?
cards.loop: Pause one chosen contribution briefly and observe whether the pattern changes.

cards.title: Shadow Benefit
cards.mirror: Does the current pattern provide protection or familiarity, or are exhaustion and limited resources sufficient explanations?
cards.loop: Preserve one suspected protection while changing a small part of the pattern.

cards.title: Expired Vow
cards.mirror: When a repeated commitment outlasts its original context, is it carrying a core value—or serving a present duty?
cards.loop: Try one low-stakes variation; note whether integrity strengthens, weakens, or stays unchanged.

cards.title: Aligned Agreement
cards.mirror: Which agreements support a chosen direction while remaining workable for present needs, uncertainty, and reciprocal commitments?
cards.loop: Trial one agreement briefly, then review its benefits, costs, and effects on others.

cards.title: Shadow Integration
cards.mirror: Which commitments repeatedly collide, and would coordination help more than forcing them into complete agreement?
cards.loop: Give two competing commitments one temporary coordination rule and observe the next collision.

cards.title: New Covenant
cards.mirror: Which deep commitment appears to shape repeated choices, alongside habits, relationships, resources, and surrounding structures?
cards.loop: Make one revisable covenant for a week, then compare intention with observable choices.

cards.title: Inherited Desire
cards.mirror: Which desires recur across changing contexts, and which appear mainly around particular expectations, relationships, or roles?
cards.loop: Optionally compare one desire across three contexts, noting both personal meaning and outside influence.

cards.title: Desire Echo
cards.mirror: Does an older desire still create meaningful engagement, or does it persist mainly through routine and remembered importance?
cards.loop: Revisit one old desire briefly, then compare anticipation, engagement, and aftereffects.

cards.title: Desire Pulse
cards.mirror: Which possibilities repeatedly bring steadier attention or vitality, and what other evidence agrees or conflicts with that pulse?
cards.loop: Try one small step, then compare bodily response, consequences, values, and practical context.

cards.title: Desire Purity
cards.mirror: Clarity may emerge by distinguishing overlapping influences, not by finding one perfectly uncontaminated desire.
cards.loop: Map one desire’s influences, then test which combination remains workable and meaningful.

cards.title: Desire Distortion
cards.mirror: When a desired option changes near risk or uncertainty, fear may be involved—but so may values, limits, or judgment.
cards.loop: Compare the option under one safer condition and observe whether its appeal meaningfully changes.

cards.title: Desire Geometry
cards.mirror: Imagine desire as a shape: do its scale, boundaries, timing, and costs fit the life presently anticipated?
cards.loop: Redraw one desire at two scales, then compare feasibility, meaning, and consequences.

cards.title: True Want
cards.mirror: A meaningful want may remain complex after fear, history, obligation, and imagined futures are examined.
cards.loop: Let present and imagined future perspectives evaluate one small, reversible choice.

cards.title: Desire Vector
cards.mirror: Across repeated choices, does desire suggest a direction, several competing vectors, or no stable path yet?
cards.loop: Test one possible direction with a bounded step and compare desire, duty, and consequence.

cards.title: Desire Conflict
cards.mirror: A difficult choice may contain several legitimate interests, not merely a contest between growth and safety.
cards.loop: Compare two reversible trials using values, costs, safety, growth, and affected relationships.

cards.title: Curated Desire
cards.mirror: Notice how a desire changes under encouragement, friction, dissent, and distance—not only under supportive exposure.
cards.loop: Curate one week of support plus deliberate counterevidence, then reassess the desire.

cards.title: Future Desire
cards.mirror: An imagined future can illuminate desire when its picture is compared with past lessons and present constraints.
cards.loop: Ask two possible future perspectives to assess one reversible choice, then compare their assumptions.

cards.title: Desire Alignment
cards.mirror: Alignment may appear gradually when desire, chosen direction, consequences, relationships, and circumstances remain workable together.
cards.loop: Run one small aligned choice, then observe coherence, costs, and effects beyond self-construction.

cards.title: Broken Agency
cards.mirror: A clear plan can coexist with repeated difficulty beginning, continuing, or completing the next visible action.
cards.loop: Test one small action while changing a single source of friction.

cards.title: Borrowed Will
cards.mirror: Action may come more readily under observation, while private follow-through reveals what accountability is actually providing.
cards.loop: Repeat one small task once observed and once privately.

cards.title: First Strike
cards.mirror: One bounded first move may reveal whether planning is preparing action or repeatedly postponing contact with reality.
cards.loop: Make one reversible move, then inspect what it teaches.

cards.title: Agency Signal
cards.mirror: Chosen action may coincide with recognizable cues such as steadier breathing, reduced hesitation, alertness, or no distinct sensation.
cards.loop: Compare bodily cues before, during, and after one chosen action.

cards.title: Fragmented Will
cards.mirror: Effort spread across competing commitments can resemble weak will, though unclear priorities or limited resources may produce the same pattern.
cards.loop: Pause one low-priority demand and observe where effort moves.

cards.title: Non-Negotiable Core
cards.mirror: A small chosen core can steady decisions when it guides tradeoffs without becoming immune to evidence or changing conditions.
cards.loop: Test one commitment alongside a clear condition for revision.

cards.title: Agency Pivot
cards.mirror: A directional pivot may expose whether stalled action comes from the current path or from constraints that direction alone cannot solve.
cards.loop: Try one bounded pivot with a checkpoint before escalation.

cards.title: Agency Channel
cards.mirror: When several commitments compete, does progress sharpen after one channel is temporarily narrowed?
cards.loop: Optionally pause one low-stakes commitment for seven days and compare completion, delay, and strain.

cards.title: Sovereign Choice
cards.mirror: A choice can remain internally owned while still drawing on consultation, expertise, uncertainty, or genuinely shared authority.
cards.loop: Make one low-stakes choice after separating advice from authority.

cards.title: Reforged Will
cards.mirror: Effort may last differently when shaped by chosen direction, external pressure, task design, available support, or their combination.
cards.loop: Compare two motivations on one repeated, low-stakes task.

cards.title: Unbreakable Direction
cards.mirror: Direction can remain durable while strategy changes, provided new evidence is allowed to challenge both means and underlying assumptions.
cards.loop: Name one fixed purpose, one revisable strategy, and one review trigger.

cards.title: Forged Agency
cards.mirror: Trust in future action can grow from repeated follow-through and repair, without requiring flawless consistency or a permanent trait.
cards.loop: Track one small promise, including completion, lapse, and repair.

cards.title: Identity Tension
cards.mirror: Notice when two credible ways of acting compete, while leaving room for coexistence rather than a forced winner.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: let both positions shape one small, reversible choice.

cards.title: Identity Residue
cards.mirror: An earlier role may still appear in present choices, whether as useful continuity, outdated habit, or unresolved attachment.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: retain, revise, and release one small element on trial.

cards.title: Identity Merge
cards.mirror: Previously conflicting priorities may now cooperate in some choices, even while meaningful differences remain elsewhere.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: test one decision for partial cooperation without demanding complete harmony.

cards.title: Synthesis Field
cards.mirror: Several changes may feel simultaneous when choices, boundaries, desires, and commitments begin affecting the same everyday situations.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: map one recent event across several changing areas.

cards.title: Geometry of Convergence
cards.mirror: Identity geometry can picture how commitments fit, where boundaries hold, and which arrangements remain flexible under pressure.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: sketch one commitment, boundary, and adjustable edge.

cards.title: Identity Resonance
cards.mirror: Resonance may describe the felt fit between stated priorities, repeated actions, and settings that make those actions easier.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: compare one aligned action across two different settings.

cards.title: True Identity
cards.mirror: An emerging possibility may feel both unfamiliar and recognizable, without proving it was hidden, destined, or final.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: inhabit one promising quality for a limited trial.

cards.title: Identity Lock
cards.mirror: Repeated supportive choices can stabilize an identity pattern while leaving it open to recurrence, revision, and changing conditions.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: repeat one supportive practice three times, then reassess.

cards.title: Identity Home
cards.mirror: A sense of home may appear when values, actions, boundaries, and present conditions become mutually livable.
cards.loop: Optionally compare what makes two contrasting moments feel more or less habitable.

cards.title: Identity Flow
cards.mirror: Flow may become visible when clarified direction changes hesitation while effort, task difficulty, and conditions remain comparable.
cards.loop: Optionally compare two similar steps, clarifying direction only before the second.

cards.title: Architect Self
cards.mirror: The architect image highlights choices, structures, and responses within influence, while conditions, other people, and chance remain active.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: redesign one controllable feature while naming three constraints.

cards.title: Final Integration
cards.mirror: Integration may look like several values, roles, and commitments coordinating for now without becoming one permanent or seamless identity.
cards.loop: Optional experiment: test coordination across one meaningful, reversible decision.
